column1: # Selective mutation campaign: batch definitions.
# One row per named batch. Batches partition the mutant census of the selected
# files exactly: every generated mutant belongs to exactly one batch, and no
# mutant belongs to two. `scripts/mutation-campaign.sh verify` proves that
# property for the current revision before any batch runs.
# Columns (tab separated):
#   1 name          stable batch identifier, used for output directories
#   2 files         --file glob
#   3 select        regex passed to --re, or "-" for the whole file census
#   4 test_filter   positional cargo test filter for stage 1, or "-" for none
#   5 rationale     short reason the batch exists
# Stage 1 runs each batch against the focused filter in column 4. Stage 2
# re-runs every stage-1 survivor against the complete unit-test suite. A narrow
# filter can over-report survivors; it cannot fabricate a kill, so stage 1 is
# sound as a pre-filter and stage 2 is the reported result.
